As someone working in a DevOps environment, I recently started diving into the world of Linux commands—and wow, it’s been a revelation! Whether you’re setting up CI/CD pipelines, configuring servers, or managing Docker containers, Linux is at the heart of everything DevOps. But here's the twist: I work on a Windows machine. The answer is: WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux). 🐧 Why WSL is a Blessing for DevOps Engineers on Windows Benefits: Run Linux CLI tools natively Use bash scripts, SSH, Git, Docker, etc. Access both Linux and Windows files Faster and lighter than a VM If you're a DevOps engineer using Windows, WSL is your best friend! 🧠 Linux Commands I Learned (and Why They Matter) cd – Change Directory
ls – List Files and Directories
grep – Search Text in Files
tail – View the End of a File
chmod and chown – Manage Permissions
ps and kill – Manage Processes
df and du – Check Disk Space
scp and ssh – Secure Copy and Remote Access
docker – Container Management
⚡ Pro Tip: Combine Commands for Superpowers ps aux | grep nginx | awk '{print $2}' | xargs kill -9 ✨ Final Thoughts The more you use it, the more natural it becomes—and the more effective you’ll be in managing infrastructure, automating tasks, and solving real-world problems.
